model: adult mouse transverse-aortic-constriction pressure-overload fibrosis followed by physical unloading

paper.title: Mechanisms that limit regression of myocardial fibrosis following removal of left ventricular pressure overload
paper.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Heart and Circulatory Physiology

causal_root.established_state: pressure-overload hypertrophy with interstitial fibrosis, elevated myocardial stiffness, increased LV wall thickness/mass, elevated aortic velocity and peak systolic stress
causal_root.delayed_intervention: surgical removal of the constricting band after 4 weeks (unTAC)

C1_DELAYED_AFTER_ESTABLISHMENT.basis: The intervention starts only after 4 weeks of TAC. The same experimental root documents the pre-unloading state with increased LV mass/wall thickness, fibrillar collagen, myocardial stiffness and hemodynamic load.

C2_DIRECT_PHYSICAL_RETUNING.basis: unTAC physically removes the aortic constriction and directly normalizes the imposed pressure load; it is not a downstream molecular surrogate.

C3_PHYSICAL_STATE_MEASURED.basis: The same root quantifies peak aortic velocity, calculated LV peak systolic stress and passive myocardial stiffness in the 4-week TAC state and at multiple post-unTAC endpoints.

C4_SAME_STATE_TRAJECTORY.basis: The same root follows the endogenous fibrotic ECM state across 4-week TAC and 2-, 4- and 6-week unTAC using collagen volume fraction, collagen-hybridizing-peptide reactivity, collagenases/gelatinases, TIMP1 and collagen-crosslinking enzymes. This is a serial scar/fibrosis-resolution trajectory under the frozen C4 alternative.

C5_TISSUE_OUTCOME_WITH_INTEGRITY.basis: After unloading, LV mass and wall thickness regress, lung/body-weight congestion falls, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy regresses and LV peak systolic stress returns toward control while EF remains stable. The measured structural/hemodynamic phenotype shows reverse remodeling rather than mechanical destabilization. The criterion is satisfied by structural outcome; no EF improvement is claimed.

myocardial_stiffness_beta.note: The paper reports progressive reduction after unTAC, with stiffness remaining above control; do not interpret these group means as an individual longitudinal decay curve.

LV_EF_percent.boundary: EF did not materially improve; C5 is supported by structural/hemodynamic reverse remodeling, not an EF rescue claim.

resolution_kinetics.early_2wk_unTAC: collagen hybridizing peptide reactivity and ECM-degrading enzymes increase while collagen volume fraction has not yet fallen substantially
resolution_kinetics.later_4wk_unTAC: collagen volume fraction decreases but remains above control; myocardial stiffness is lower than at 4-week TAC
resolution_kinetics.6wk_unTAC: fibrosis and stiffness remain incompletely normalized and late ECM-degradation activity is dampened
resolution_kinetics.interpretation: Physical unloading starts a time-ordered ECM reversal program with an early degradation phase followed by incomplete later regression.

clock_interpretation.strongest_claim: After a chronic pressure-overload fibrotic state is established, direct physical unloading causally shifts myocardial mechanical and fibrotic trajectories in a time-dependent manner within one experimental root.
not_claimed: This is not a myocardial-infarction wound-healing model and must not be represented as post-MI scar resolution.
This does not establish a universal stiffness target or a universal softer-is-better rule.
The group-wise 2/4/6-week endpoints are not an individual-tissue half-life measurement.
This does not establish lineage-resolved myofibroblast EXIT kinetics.

relation_to_exit_clock.reason: The root provides a collagen/fibrosis-resolution trajectory but not lineage-resolved activated-fibroblast clearance/apoptosis.
